title: Atelier — build the museum lantern from a blueprint
brief: Model a hanging museum lantern in Blender, by script only, from a blueprint: three orthographic silhouettes, a dimension sheet, a material sheet and a part list. Glass panes, a metal frame, a ring handle, a candle with an emissive flame, and a hinged door with an 'door_open' action. The result is exported to glTF and placed in the museum.

generator.description: One seed per benchmark version, the same for every agent (comparability). The hidden reference builder hidden/atelier/reference_build.py creates the true lantern for the seed; the harness renders the blueprint and the hidden views from it. The agent never receives the parameter list — only drawings and sheets.

hidden_params.door_side: which face carries the door; hinge on its left or right vertical frame bar

files.front.png: orthographic silhouette, 2048x2048, 0.25 mm/px, with scale bar
files.dimensions.json: overall bbox (mm), handle ring inner diameter, frame bar section, door face index and hinge side, door opening angle (90 deg), origin rule
files.materials.json: per part: OKLCH base color swatch, metallic, roughness range, transmission/IOR for glass, emission color/strength for flame
files.parts.json: required object names and parent hierarchy, which parts must be watertight
files.budget.json: triangle budget (default 30000), texture budget (<= 2 textures, <= 1024 px)

blueprint.origin_rule: Lantern root origin at the bottom center of the base, lowest point at z = 0 (Blender Z-up), all object scales applied (1,1,1).

capture.renderer: Blender Cycles CPU, pinned version, fixed seed, 128 samples, denoiser off, single fixed thread count
capture.studio_scene: harness/blender/studio.blend (3-point lights + CC0 HDRI, neutral grey backdrop); submission is linked in, never edited
capture.hidden_views: 8 oblique orthographic views (azimuth 0..315 step 45, elevation +25) + 4 from below (elevation -30); used only by shape.iou_hidden
capture.turntable: 8 perspective beauty renders at 1024x1024 for visual metrics and the Judge Console
capture.web_check: the .glb is also loaded into the lobby's three.js pedestal scene under SwiftShader

extra_gates.G-blender-run: build.py exits 0 within 120 s and writes both out/ files
extra_gates.G-reproducible: re-running build.py produces a .glb whose geometry hash (positions quantized to 0.01 mm, indices, per-primitive material names) equals the submitted one
extra_gates.G-provenance: no imports of mesh/scene files outside blueprint/ or assets/ (runtime hook on bpy.ops.import_* and bpy.data.libraries.load)

metrics.notes: the real modeling test: matching three views is not enough
handle ring inner diameter ±2%, frame bar section ±10%, pane count exact, door on the specified face
non-manifold edges on parts flagged watertight in parts.json
only for parts that use a texture
hard 90-degree metal edges catch no light and look CG
only if textures are used; otherwise weight drops out
mean L of object pixels in turntable renders under the fixed studio light
fraction of metal pixels with L > 0.85 (metals read as metal)

hidden_tests: Flame material is emissive and Flame casts no shadow-blocking geometry over the glass (Flame is excluded or tiny)
Glass panes are single objects per pane or one 'Glass' object with thickness >= 1 mm (not zero-thickness planes)
Door_Glass moves with Door during door_open
glb loads in three.js with <= 12 draw calls and no console errors
attacks: three-view-extrusion: intersection of the three silhouettes extruded (perfect public IoU) — shape.iou_hidden and dims.key_measurements must pull composite <= 4
single-blob: one unnamed mesh with correct outline, no hierarchy, no hinge — must score composite <= 4
dense-mesh: 2M-triangle subdivided model — budget.triangles and web.three_load must pull composite <= 5
